No photo shows the system specifications, BIOS, or any internal component. The CPU model cannot be confirmed from the exterior.

risks.risk: The laptop may not have the advertised Intel Core i5 8th generation processor
risks.proof: A photo of the system information screen (Windows About or BIOS) showing the CPU model.
risks.if_unproven: priced as if it has a lower-end or non-existent CPU, reducing value significantly

risks.risk: The laptop may have hidden physical damage or wear not visible in photos
risks.proof: A 360-degree video or close-up photos of all edges, hinges, screen bezel, and ports.
risks.if_unproven: priced as if it has moderate wear or damage, reducing value

risks.risk: The laptop may be non-functional or have software issues (e.g., missing OS, malware, or activation problems)
risks.proof: A video showing the laptop booting up, logging into Windows, and running a simple task (e.g., opening a browser).
risks.if_unproven: priced as if it does not work, reducing value to scrap or parts level

risks.risk: The laptop may be stolen or have a blacklisted serial number
risks.proof: A photo of the serial number sticker (usually on the bottom) and a verification from a trusted source (e.g., HP support or IMEI checker).
risks.if_unproven: priced as if it is at risk of being seized or unusable, reducing value

proof_requests: A photo of the system information screen showing the CPU model and specs.
A video of the laptop booting up and running Windows smoothly.
A close-up photo of the serial number sticker on the bottom of the laptop.
A 360-degree photo or video showing all sides, hinges, and ports for damage assessment.
